synopsis: Resources Safety and Health Queensland publishes QGN 27, its 2017 guidance on collision prevention [f15541]. Chapter 4 and the glossary both report its finding that collisions accounted for 26% of mineral mine and quarry fatalities between 1998 and 2016 [f3103, f15542]. QGN 27 identifies vehicle-to-vehicle, vehicle-to-person and vehicle-to-infrastructure interactions as important high-potential incident classes, with a loader striking a pedestrian on a roadway as a worked critical-risk scenario [f3104, f3105]. Its worked stopping example shows a machine travelling 22.2 m at 40 km/h during a 2 s reaction-plus-delay period, while its warning about idealized detection zones cautions against a false sense of protection [f15543, f15544].

relations.note: Both report the same collision fatality share and reporting period.
The loader–pedestrian scenario exemplifies the vehicle-to-person incident class.
Distance travelled during reaction and delay reinforces caution about assumed detection-zone protection.
